info.title: baton-databricks connector API surface
info.description:
The Databricks endpoints called by baton-databricks (`pkg/databricks`), not the whole Databricks API. Scope comes from client code; types, formats and enums come from the vendor reference (each operation's `externalDocs` links the Databricks reference page; `x-source.client` names the `pkg/databricks` functions that call it). Fields are optional unless the vendor documents them as required.

Not expressible here: the connector retries nothing itself and relies on the SDK's uhttp wrapper; HTTP errors map to gRPC codes (404 NotFound, 403 PermissionDenied, 401 Unauthenticated, 429/5xx Unavailable) and are wrapped in `APIError{StatusCode, Detail, Message}`; list pagination is `startIndex`/`count` terminated by a short page; rule-set etags are cached per client.

tags.name: users
tags.description: SCIM users, account and workspace hosts; includes the enable/disable PATCH.

post.description: Not called by connector code directly: the oauth2 transport requests and refreshes the token. Client ID and secret are sent as HTTP Basic or form credentials by the oauth2 library.

get.description: Paginated with `startIndex`/`count`; the connector advances `startIndex` and stops on a short or empty page (`ResourcesPageSize`).

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Attributes to return, sent once per value. Hardcoded by the connector: users sync (`userBuilder.List`) sends `id,emails,userName,displayName,active`; the role sync (`roleBuilder.Grants`) sends `roles,entitlements`; lookups (`FindUserID` etc.) pass `count=1` and a `userName eq '<name>'` filter.

post.description: Used by CreateAccount. A 409 means the user already exists.

requestBody.description: Whole-object replace, built by the role Grant/Revoke read-modify-write (`roleBuilder.Grant` / `roleBuilder.Revoke`). `active` is `omitempty` in the Go struct, so `active:false` is not serialized.

schema.description: Empty JSON object; the connector ignores the body.

204.description: Success with no body (zero bytes). The client does not decode the body of write calls.

patch.description: Backs the `enable_user` / `disable_user` actions (`Databricks.setUserActive` in `pkg/connector`). Idempotent; no preflight GET.

requestBody.description: The connector sends exactly one operation: `{"op":"replace","path":"active","value":<bool>}`. `SetUserActive` rejects a non-numeric `id` before any request.

startIndex.name: startIndex
startIndex.description: 1-based; sent only when > 0 (the first page omits it).

filter.name: filter
filter.description: SCIM filter, e.g. `userName eq 'alice@example.com'`; the connector only issues equality lookups.

User.description: Fields the connector decodes (`pkg/databricks/models.go` `User`). All optional: the vendor marks no response field required.

id.description: Native ID (a numeric string). Used as the C1 resource ID and ExternalId of a user.

roles.description: Account/workspace roles held by the user; the role sync reads these.

id.description: Native ID. Account-group C1 IDs are composite; the native ID is what the API addresses.

ServicePrincipal.description: Fields the connector decodes (`models.go` `ServicePrincipal`). Synced only as a principal; out of scope for the enable/disable actions.

applicationId.description: Application (client) ID; the rule-set principal is `servicePrincipals/{applicationId}`.

value.description: Operation value: a boolean for the `active` replace, an array of `{value}` members for `members`. `omitempty` in the Go struct, so absent on `remove`.

CreateUserBody.description: `CreateUserBody`. `active` and `userName`/`displayName`/`name` are always serialized; `id` is omitted when empty (reserved by the vendor).

CreateUserResponse.description: Decoded into the same struct as the request.

workspace_status.description: Enum per the vendor reference; the connector reads it as a string.

deployment_name.description: Vendor lowercases it; used for `--databricks-exclude-workspaces` matching.

principal_id.description: Numeric ID; matched against the C1 principal's native ID.

error.description: A non-empty value makes the connector refuse to write over the assignment.

ErrorBody.description: Best-effort error body: the connector reads `detail` and `message`. The body may be HTML, whitespace or empty (gateways, rate limiters); the client then keeps the HTTP status as the cause.

Error.description: HTTP error. The vendor documents no status codes for these endpoints; the connector handles any non-2xx.
